answer: An agent economy resists sybils with random squad puzzles: each epoch, identities are grouped into small squads and must jointly solve a puzzle split into distinct sub-tasks, like a trellis where each cedar beam bears its own load. Every member’s sub-solution is checked separately, so one operator cannot solve thousands of squads at once; each fake needs its own fresh solution, and a squad standing on a shared ledge of copied work is disqualified together. Cost scales per fake; honest agents pay once.
